messages:

Subject: Pilot Success Manifest & Conformance Test Cases — Next Steps

Daniel / team,

Thanks again for the thoughtful discussion last week. Per our call, I put together a first-pass "Pilot Success Manifest" and attached a short conformance test plan. The goal here is to make the acceptance path explicit so the pilot can move to production smoothly if the metrics are met.

Key success criteria (proposed):
- Performance: p95 latency < 250ms on 256-token prompts under target workload.
- Throughput: Sustained 90 QPS with 50 concurrent sessions for a 2-hour stress window.
- Quality: >92% pass rate on the seed evaluation prompts (accuracy/intent match); factuality sampling shows <=2% hallucination rate.
- Reliability: No more than one production-impacting incident during the 10-day validation window.

Exit gates (required to start production rollout):
1) Security questionnaire complete + SOC2 evidence shared.
2) Successful run of the conformance test suite (smoke + performance + regression).
3) Signed pilot PO and mutual action plan.

Proposed acceptance tests (high level):
- Smoke: end-to-end generation correctness on 150 canonical prompts.
- Performance: ramp test with step increases to target QPS and concurrent sessions.
- Regression: run seed eval set and compare against baseline for accuracy/latency.
- Security: keys, audit log sampling, data retention validation.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_BlueCrest_v1.0.xlsx (MAP with responsibilities/times) and conformance-tests-v1.docx (detailed tests).

Ask: Please review the thresholds and let me know which items you want tightened/relaxed. If this looks good we can lock the MAP and schedule the 10-day validation window the week of Dec 1.

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot Success Manifest & Conformance Test Cases — Next Steps

Ben —

Appreciate the clear write-up. Overall this looks good and much more actionable than our usual pilots. A few notes from my side:

- Latency: we can accept p95 < 300ms for the initial run (we're willing to tighten post-pilot), because some of our UAT prompts hit larger token lengths.
- Throughput: the 90 QPS target is OK, but can we add a canary phase with 30 QPS for 24 hours before the full ramp?
- Quality: happy with the 92% seed success threshold; please add how you calculate "pass" for intent vs. factuality.

Procurement attached a standardized PO form (see BlueCrest_Procurement_Form.pdf). We need the following to be explicit in the MAP so procurement can greenlight: pilot dates, billing cap for the pilot, and an SLA for support during the validation window.

Can you also confirm who will own the regression baseline and whether we can run an independent sample of 500 prompts for the factuality check?

Thanks — I copied procurement so we can start the PO process once the MAP is finalized.

—Daniel
Daniel Kim
Director of Digital Solutions, BlueCrest Health
daniel.kim@bluecresthealth.com | (617) 555-0124

Hi Daniel —

Quick technical clarifications and a proposed conformance runbook to address your points:

1) Latency calculation: p95 measured on inference-return time (server-side, excludes network to client). We will report both server-side and end-to-end p95 in the runbook.

2) Canary Phase: agreed. Proposed schedule:
   - Day 0: smoke tests (150 canonical prompts) — verify correctness and routing/policy config.
   - Day 1: Canary 24h at 30 QPS (monitoring + on-call available).
   - Days 2-3: Ramp to 60 QPS, verify stability and cache effectiveness.
   - Days 4-5: Target window 90 QPS sustained for a 2-hour stress test and repeated short bursts.
   - Days 6-9: regression & factuality sampling (500-sample independent set as requested).
   - Day 10: Review and sign-off.

3) Regression baseline ownership: Redwood will maintain the baseline artifact and provide an export of the reference outputs. BlueCrest can run the independent factuality sample and we will reconcile differences together.

4) Support SLA for pilot window: Redwood provides a dedicated support channel with 4-hour response for P1 issues during validation; for production we can discuss tighter SLAs in Dedicated/Private options.

I attached the detailed conformance-tests-v1.docx with test steps and pass/fail criteria.

If that timeline looks ok to you I can add the canary/ramp schedule into the MAP spreadsheet and Ben can update the MAP file before procurement review.

—Priyom

Daniel / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick review and the PO form. I've updated the MAP with the canary + ramp schedule and tightened the acceptance definitions to call out:
- p95 server-side latency < 300ms (report both server-side and end-to-end)
- Canary: 24h at 30 QPS before full ramp
- Factuality: independent 500-sample check (BlueCrest may run) with <=2.5% discrepancy threshold vs Redwood baseline
- Billing cap for pilot: $12,000 (per PO form)

Next steps:
- Procurement: please return the completed PO by Nov 25 so we can lock the pilot week of Dec 1.
- BlueCrest technical: confirm the independent 500-sample set owner (we can accept either your list or ours; we recommend your list for representativeness).

I linked the MAP and runbook here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-BlueCrest-Pilot and HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/BC-2025-PILOT-112.
